basis: check_commit() declares its arguments as (ROOT, REV) and the `case` dispatcher passed them the other way round, so the documented invocation `--check-commit [REV]` put the revision into the ROOT slot. git -C <not-a-directory> rev-list prints nothing on stdout, the empty rev list was read as 'no commits in HEAD', and the guard exited 0 without looking at a single commit. b126d7d fixed glob_match() -- the engine -- and recorded that check_commit() flagged zero paths across all 11 commits; the wiring was a separate defect and stayed reversed, so the documented command remained fail-open. Three changes, all strengthening, none widening scope: (1) the dispatcher now passes (ROOT, REV) in the order the function declares, ROOT coming from this script's own location as ROOT_DEFAULT always intended; (2) a ROOT that is not a repository and a range git cannot resolve are now exit 2, because the old code could not distinguish 'the range selected nothing' from 'I read nothing at all' and answered both with exit 0; (3) git diff-tree gains --root, without which a repository's first commit is invisible to the check entirely -- live here, where root commit 1f43c9e adds ten R2 paths and not one was ever reported. Assertions 11a-11d run the script as a SUBPROCESS from inside a fixture repository with ONE argument, because every pre-existing assertion calls guard()/check_commit() directly and therefore cannot see the dispatcher -- that is how this defect survived a fix already reported complete. GUARDED_PATHS and REVIEW_REQUIRED_PATHS are byte-identical to the previous revision: this is a wiring fix, not a scope change. No change to scripts/retention-literal-gate.sh or scripts/run-db-tests.mjs. No migration, no engine change, no personal data, so the CTO migration-approval path is not engaged.
